newsitem.title: UK: UK housing sales leapt in Jan - Inland Revenue.
newsitem.headline: UK housing sales leapt in Jan - Inland Revenue.

text.p: Britain's Inland Revenue said the number of houses sold in January leapt to their highest monthly level since 1992.
The number of property transactions totalled 132,000 in England and Wales on an unadjusted basis in the first month of the year, compared with 109,000 in December and 104,000 in January last year.
On a seasonally adjusted basis, 123,000 properties were sold compared with 120,000 in December and 97,000 in January 1996.
Although the figures cover property transactions as a whole, about 90 percent of the sales relates to housing.
Not since an unadjusted 143,000 property transactions took place in September 1992 has activity been higher in any one month, Inland Revenue figures showed.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders welcomed the news but warned that one swallow might not make a summer. "Although it can be misleading to place too much emphasis on one month's figures, this most recent data does confirm that transaction activity is now in line with the firming in house prices already experienced," said CML director general Michael Coogan.

Britain's housing market has been suffering from a chronic shortage of properties to buy. In certain areas -- particularly London and the South East -- prices have squeezed through the roof as a result.
"This will produce a sound and sustainable housing market recovery without the risk of overheating," Coogan said.
